title: A process record left behind by a reboot no longer blocks a runtime's stop, roll or start
kind: code and tests only; no Docker engine, runtime, process or provider was used
gap: After a reboot, a recorded PID held by an unrelated process made ownedProcess throw 'PID identity changed',
so every stop, roll and start of that runtime refused until the record was moved by hand.

decisions.D1: Recorded PID held by a process with another CreationDate: the recorded one exited; null is returned.
D2: That record is renamed aside, never deleted, to <label>.process.json.exited-<yyyyMMddHHmmss> (UTC).
One line names the label and both creation dates only. A later launchProcesses writes a fresh record.
decisions.D3: Same CreationDate with another command line, executable, entry or preload: refused with the same words.
D4: Record shape, ports and spawning are unchanged.
ownedProcess takes an optional third argument { info } (default processInfo) so tests stand in for it.

skippedBothTimes: dry-run frozen profiles pass existing verifiedProfile only for the exact repo, hash and interpreter
the CLI switch passes the real import preflight with the project-owned interpreter, on a copy

newTests: Same PID, other CreationDate: null; old name gone; one aside copy with the same bytes; one line printed.
Same CreationDate, other entry, executable or preload: the same refusal; the record stays.
No process holds the PID: null. A matching process: the record. Neither moves the record.
